items.title: Geoff Wilkinson, Ontario Traffic Council
notes: G. Wilkinson, Executive Director, Ontario Traffic Council, appeared before the Committee to speak about Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE). He expressed support for the program, providing information on its safety benefits, the impact of speeding, and its role in injury prevention. He also discussed potential improvements to ASE and urged the Committee to maintain the program in Ontario to help keep children safe in school zones.

Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
COR-CFN-25-015, 2025 Reserve Fund Update
notes:
Wayne Steffler, Commissioner, Corporate Services and Chief Financial Officer, introduced the report. Nicole Neil, Director, Corporate Finance, delivered a presentation outlining the types of reserves, obligatory reserves, reserve health, and next steps. A copy of the presentation is appended to the original agenda.

In response to questions from the Committee, N. Neil provided clarification on several reserves, including the Accessible Reserve and the Facilities Lifecycle Reserve, outlining their purposes and confirming she would follow up with additional details where needed. She explained that contributions to the Facilities Lifecycle Reserve support ongoing building maintenance and renewal.

Members also asked about how best practices are determined, the limits of reserve funds, and eligibility for the Brownfields Reserve. N. Neil explained that contingency levels are based on industry-wide standards and that the Brownfields Reserve applies to projects already approved by the Region. Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development and Legislative Services, added that as of January 1, the Region became ineligible to participate in the Community Improvement Plan (CIP) for Brownfields, as this responsibility now rests with the area municipalities. He noted that no applications have been accepted since that date and the Region is awaiting further provincial direction.

Committee members further discussed how the Region plans for infrastructure funding to support housing development. N. Neil explained that growth-related needs are identified in the Region’s Master Plans and are funded as quickly as possible, acknowledging the challenges associated with Bill 17. She noted that staff are reviewing the timing and reprofiling of growth projects to ensure realistic delivery schedules, with updates anticipated as part of the 2027 budget process. Acting Chief Administrative Officer Mathieu Goetzke added that future coordination with major initiatives, such as the Cambridge LRT extension, will continue to be assessed.

Questions were also raised about the Housing Reserve and whether it functions as a revolving loan. N. Neil clarified that it represents savings against a loan and committed to providing additional information.

In response to a final question about LRT funding, W. Steffler confirmed that the 2025 budget included debt funding for the project, which is under review for the 2026 budget. He emphasized that the Region’s financial planning and infrastructure investment must continue to align with the pace of regional growth.

items.title: Notice of Motion - Councillor C. James
notes:
C. James introduced her Notice of Motion, noting that Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) was implemented to improve community safety. She emphasized the need to carefully consider the implications of any changes to the program and recommended that the Region continue operating the existing ASE program until further direction is received from the Province and updated legislation is in place. She also suggested pausing any program expansion until that time.

In response to questions from the Committee, Doug Spooner, Commissioner, Transportation Services, stated that there were no significant risks or financial penalties associated with temporarily pausing the expansion. He explained that ASE is administered in accordance with provincial regulations and Council direction, noting that 22 school zones currently have cameras in operation, with six additional sites ready to go live this week. Under the proposed motion, those six sites would not proceed at this time.

An amendment was proposed by P. Wolf to limit ASE ticketing to school operating hours and apply fines only to vehicles significantly exceeding the speed limit. The Committee discussed the amendment, focusing on road safety, fairness, and the intent of ASE. Following deliberation, the amendment was defeated.

The Committee then returned to the main motion and continued discussion regarding program funding, transparency, and road safety on Regional roads. In response to further questions, D. Spooner confirmed that minimal costs would be incurred if the six new cameras were paused and provided an overview of their planned locations.

A subsequent amendment was introduced by J. Liggett to allow the installation of the six planned cameras to proceed. Following discussion, this amendment carried.

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - Councillor C. James
motions.text: WHEREAS The Region of Waterloo is in the midst of enacting an automated speed enforcement plan rooted in changing driver behaviour, increasing public safety, and saving lives following a pilot program that began in 2021; WHEREAS Ontario’s Premier Doug Ford publicly announced the intention to ban automated speed enforcement province-wide in forthcoming legislation; WHEREAS details remain limited of such a bill or legislation and next steps for municipal operators of automated speed enforcement are unclear; WHEREAS The Region of Waterloo has invested significantly in automated speed enforcement, with a program committed to expanding speed cameras to all eligible schools across Waterloo Region by 2028, and is heading into budget deliberations for 2026; WHEREAS automated speed enforcement cameras generate an 87% drop in number of vehicles driving more than 20km/h over the speed limit (source: SickKids/TMU study, July 2025 and that in Waterloo Region, the 85th percentile speed has decreased by over 16km/h on average in school zones covered by a speed camera. THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT The Region of Waterloo halt any further previously planned expansion, AT 28 SCHOOL ZONES, of the automated speed enforcement program until details of the pending legislation are made available. The Region of Waterloo halt any further hiring of staff to deliver on the automated speed enforcement program and that; The Region of Waterloo maintain operation of the current automated speed enforcement program as-is today to provide clarity for drivers, community members, pedestrians, and staff and that; Regional Council requests Region of Waterloo staff report back to Council on the implications of ending the automated speed enforcement program in the Region of Waterloo pending forthcoming Provincial legislation.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS The Region of Waterloo is in the midst of enacting an automated speed enforcement plan rooted in changing driver behaviour, increasing public safety, and saving lives following a pilot program that began in 2021;

WHEREAS Ontario’s Premier Doug Ford publicly announced the intention to ban automated speed enforcement province-wide in forthcoming legislation;

WHEREAS details remain limited of such a bill or legislation and next steps for municipal operators of automated speed enforcement are unclear;

WHEREAS The Region of Waterloo has invested significantly in automated speed enforcement, with a program committed to expanding speed cameras to all eligible schools across Waterloo Region by 2028, and is heading into budget deliberations for 2026;

WHEREAS automated speed enforcement cameras generate an 87% drop in number of vehicles driving more than 20km/h over the speed limit (source: SickKids/TMU study, July 2025 and that in Waterloo Region, the 85th percentile speed has decreased by over 16km/h on average in school zones covered by a speed camera.

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT

The Region of Waterloo halt any further previously planned expansion, AT 28 SCHOOL ZONES, of the automated speed enforcement program until details of the pending legislation are made available.

The Region of Waterloo halt any further hiring of staff to deliver on the automated speed enforcement program and that;

The Region of Waterloo maintain operation of the current automated speed enforcement program as-is today to provide clarity for drivers, community members, pedestrians, and staff and that;

Regional Council requests Region of Waterloo staff report back to Council on the implications of ending the automated speed enforcement program in the Region of Waterloo pending forthcoming Provincial legislation.
